summary: Tested 4 advanced features: APScheduler, PDF Export, Concurrent Bulk Scanning, WebSocket Progress. Backend: 4/4 pytest cases pass. Frontend: PDF download works end-to-end (verified 2649-byte valid PDF via UI). WebSocket connects and receives progress events. However, the 'Live' badge on Bulk Scan page never appears due to a stale-closure bug in the frontend WebSocket handler.

minor.issue: Historical AttributeError in backend logs ('str' object has no attribute .get) from an earlier version passing scan_ids strings to generate_pdf_report. Current code fetches scan docs and passes them; no longer reproducible, but logs remain.

ui_bugs.issue: 'Live' badge never renders during a running bulk scan. Stale-closure bug: connectWebSocket is a useCallback with deps [selectedBulkScan]; it is invoked immediately after setSelectedBulkScan(newScan), so the captured closure still references the OLD selectedBulkScan (null). Consequently the `if (selectedBulkScan?.id === scanId)` branch in ws.onmessage never runs on 'started'/'progress' events, so selectedBulkScan.status is never updated to 'running'. The badge condition `wsConnected && selectedBulkScan?.status === 'running'` therefore stays false. Meanwhile setBulkScans updates work, so the history list updates, and the completion toast fires (because fetchBulkScans refetches on 'completed').

action_items: Fix stale-closure in BulkScanPage.connectWebSocket: either (a) pass scanId + newScan directly and use a ref (selectedBulkScanRef) inside ws.onmessage to read the latest selectedBulkScan, (b) remove `selectedBulkScan` from the deps and always update selectedBulkScan by checking the ref, or (c) unconditionally update selectedBulkScan when its id equals scanId by using a functional setState that reads prev (already partially done - just remove the outer `if (selectedBulkScan?.id === scanId)` guard, since setSelectedBulkScan(prev => prev?.id===scanId ? {...} : prev) is safe).
Optional: clean up stale AttributeError from backend logs by verifying no callers still pass raw scan_ids into generate_pdf_report.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js is now 1957 lines - splitting into per-page components is overdue.

connectWebSocket useCallback has a subtle stale closure problem when used together with setState calls made in the same tick. Prefer a ref to selectedBulkScan (const selectedRef = useRef(); useEffect(()=>{selectedRef.current=selectedBulkScan}, [selectedBulkScan])) and use selectedRef.current inside ws.onmessage.
run_bulk_scan_job: good use of asyncio.Semaphore(5). Consider making concurrency configurable via env var.
check_scheduled_scans uses ISO string comparison for next_run <= now.isoformat() - works because ISO 8601 UTC strings compare lexicographically, but a Datetime type in Mongo would be safer.
generate_pdf_report has no exception handling; a malformed scans entry would 500 the endpoint. Wrap in try/except and return 500 with a friendly message.

success_rate.frontend: 80% (PDF works, WebSocket delivers events, but Live badge UI bug)

seed_data_creation: Created ~2 bulk scans (5 & 10 targets), 1 recon scan on example.com, 1 report during PDF test. Not cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests at /app/backend/tests/test_advanced_features.py verify all four features. Set REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL env var when running pytest. The only remaining bug is a frontend stale-closure preventing the Live badge; the underlying WebSocket protocol works fine (proven with a websockets client that receives started/progress/completed events).
rca of the issue: Live badge bug RCA: In startBulkScan, `setSelectedBulkScan(newScan)` is queued and `connectWebSocket(id)` is called synchronously right after. `connectWebSocket` is a useCallback with dependency [selectedBulkScan] - so its closure captures whatever selectedBulkScan was at render time (typically null when starting the first bulk scan). Inside ws.onmessage the code does `if (selectedBulkScan?.id === scanId) setSelectedBulkScan(prev => ...)` - the outer guard uses the stale captured value, so it evaluates to `null?.id === scanId` = false, and the setSelectedBulkScan updater is never invoked. Fix: remove the outer if-guard and rely on the functional updater's own equality check via prev, OR use a ref to always read the current selectedBulkScan.
